entries.name: context7
entries.summary: Current documentation for libraries and frameworks, looked up by name and version.
entries.why: Workers read the docs of the library version the project uses instead of what the model remembers.

entries.name: playwright
entries.summary: Drives a real browser: open pages, click, fill forms, read the page and take screenshots.
entries.why: A worker can try the web UI it just built, step by step, beyond the headless self-check.

entries.name: exa
entries.summary: Web search built for AI: returns the content of the pages it finds.
entries.why: Research and document goals get fresh, citable sources beyond the built-in web search.

entries.name: brave-search
entries.summary: Brave's independent web index: web, news and image search.
entries.why: Research and document goals get fresh sources beyond the built-in web search.

entries.name: rea
entries.summary: Reverse engineers shipped software on this computer: native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET, Android packages, websites and captures, with the evidence behind each conclusion.
entries.why: A goal can study how a reference app or an undocumented interface does something and build its own version from the evidence; research goals get a tool that reads binaries. Tools that run the target, attach a debugger or touch a connected device stay off unless Settings opens them.
entries.disclaimer: REA analyses software you own or are authorised to examine: security research, interoperability, preservation, learning how a feature works. Never use it to bypass licences, DRM or authentication, to build cheats, or to copy proprietary code; Foundry's sessions are told the same. What it finds reaches your model provider like any other context. Native binaries also need Hopper, Ghidra or IDA on this computer; everything else works without them.
